walkthroughs.body_html:
Crime & Deviance with Theory & Methods — a core area of A-Level Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Crime & Deviance with Theory & Methods brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Crime & Deviance with Theory & Methods.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the 'dark figure' of crime?
options: Organised crime by criminal masterminds.
The amount of crime that is unreported or unrecorded.
Crimes committed at night.
Because crime makes society wealthier.

mcqs.q: What is Merton's strain theory of crime?
options: Strain theory says people commit crime because they are stressed.

Crime results from a mismatch between cultural goals (success, wealth) and legitimate means of achieving them — those who can't access legitimate means may innovate (crime), ritualise, retreat or rebel.
Strain theory says criminals have psychological strain disorders.
Because crime makes society wealthier.

mcqs.q: Why did Durkheim see crime as functional?
options: Because crime makes society wealthier.
It reinforces collective values through punishment and reaction.
Strain theory says criminals have psychological strain disorders.
Because criminals provide a useful service.
